Get started

Your first mighty ADaM program

In this minimal example you build ADSL with mighty. You will:

  1. set up the study config (_mighty.yml),
  2. describe ADSL in a specification (adsl.yml),
  3. write one custom component for a derived column,
  4. call generate_adam_code(), which returns the R program that builds ADSL.

Key terms

  • Domain: one dataset, e.g. DM (SDTM) or ADSL (ADaM).
  • Specification: a YAML file describing one ADaM domain you want mighty to build, e.g. adsl.yml. mighty generates the program for every domain that has a specification.
  • External domain: a dataset the program reads but mighty doesn’t build: SDTM, metadata, or ADaM made elsewhere.
  • Keys: the columns that identify one row in a table. mighty uses them to join domains. A generated domain lists its keys in its specification; external domains list them in _mighty.yml.
  • Component: an R script or Mustache template with the code for one derivation, e.g. age_group_01.R.
  • repos: the folders or GitHub repositories where mighty looks for components, listed in _mighty.yml.
  • define.xml: the document that describes each ADaM column for regulatory submission. mighty does not create it; mighty.toolbox builds it from the same specifications.

Study directory guidelines

A mighty study looks like this:

my_study/                 <- working directory when running example_01_main.R
├── example_01_main.R
├── _connector.yml
├── study_dir/            <- mighty specifications
│   ├── _mighty.yml
│   ├── _study.yml
│   └── adsl.yml
└── components/           <- "./components" in repos
    └── age_group_01.R

study_dir/ holds only YAML files:

  • one specification per ADaM domain (e.g. adsl.yml)
  • _mighty.yml: framework configuration (keys of external datasets and component repositories)
  • _study.yml: study-level properties (optional, used by mighty.toolbox for define.xml)
  • _documents.yml, _codelists.yml: optional, read by mighty.metadata

mighty reads every other .yml file in study_dir/ as a specification. Keep other files outside it: the connector config (_connector.yml), which tells the generated programs where your data is; your custom components; and the folder you save the generated programs to.

Set up your framework configuration file

_mighty.yml holds the study-wide settings. It has two parts:

  • external_data: the keys of each external domain the programs read. mighty uses them when it joins domains. Here that is DM, the source of ADSL. ADSL’s own keys are in adsl.yml.
  • repos: where mighty looks for components (see below).

The repos field lists where mighty looks for code components. The first entry points to the standard components repo; the second is a local directory with the study-specific custom components.

_mighty.yml

external_data:
  - id: DM
    keys: [USUBJID, STUDYID]
  - id: LB
    keys: [USUBJID, STUDYID, LBSEQ]
repos:
  - "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@dev/internal-components"
  - "./components"

Set up your ADaM specification

The specification has a header describing ADSL, a population section saying the rows come from DM (keeping subjects with a known AGE), and a columns list with every column of the final dataset:

  • USUBJID, STUDYID, ARM, AGE: listed as an id, so they’re kept from DM as they are.
  • PLANNED_ARM: method: ADSL.ARM makes a copy of ARM under a new name.
  • AGE_GRP1: component means it’s derived by the custom component age_group_01.R (see next section).

Listing only columns that belong in the final dataset is a good practice that helps in keeping things tidy. See vignette("adam_specification") for everything a specification can contain.

adsl.yml

id: ADSL
label: Subject Level Analysis Dataset
class: SUBJECT LEVEL ANALYSIS DATASET
structure: One record per subject
keys: [USUBJID, STUDYID]

population:
  base:
    - domain: DM
      depends:
        - AGE
      filter: '!is.na(AGE)'
  global:
    - filter: NA
      depends:
        - NA

columns:
  - id: USUBJID

  - id: STUDYID

  - id: ARM

  - id: PLANNED_ARM
    method: ADSL.ARM

  - id: AGE

  - id: AGE_GRP1
    component:
      id: "age_group_01.R"

Define your custom component

The column AGE_GRP1 in ADSL is derived by using a custom component that contains the R logic to process the ADSL table by deriving the additional column AGE_GRP1.

Save the component in the components directory listed under repos. The ADaM specification refers to it by its file name, age_group_01.R.

Relative paths in repos are resolved against the working directory, not against the location of _mighty.yml. This example assumes R is started in my_study/, the folder that contains both study_dir/ and components/ (see the tree under Study directory guidelines).

age_group_01.R

#' @title Age group 01
#' @description Grouping of age
#' @type column
#' @origin Derived
#' @method Age cut into the groups < 18, 18-64, 65-74 and >= 75 years.
#' @depends ADSL AGE
#' @outputs AGE_GRP1
#' @returns `ADSL`
#' @code
ADSL <- ADSL |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    AGE_GRP1 = cut(
      AGE,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 18, 65, 75, Inf),
      labels = c("< 18 years", "18 - 64 years", "65 - 74 years", ">= 75 years"),
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

The #' header tells mighty what the component needs (@depends ADSL AGE) and what it creates (@outputs AGE_GRP1). The code after @code is inserted into the ADSL program as it is. See vignette("code_components") for all tags.

Render the ADaM program

Call mighty to consolidate, analyze and render your ADSL program:

path_connector_config is the path to your connector config. mighty writes this path into the generated programs, which read the file when they run.

example_01_main.R

# ADSL with 1 base domain (DM)
#   - 4 columns kept from DM
#   - 1 copied column (PLANNED_ARM)
#   - 1 derived column (AGE_GRP1)

# Load mighty
library(mighty)

# Generate ADaM program
results <- mighty::generate_adam_code(
  adam_specifications = "study_dir",
  path_connector_config = "_connector.yml"
)

# Print rendered ADaM program
results$programs$`1_ADSL` |> cat()

generate_adam_code() returns a list. Its programs element holds the generated R programs, each one a character string. Each name starts with the order to run the programs in, so here there is a single program, 1_ADSL. When a study has several domains, a domain that uses ADSL comes after it (e.g. 2_ADAE). If ADSL itself needs columns from another domain, ADSL is split into two programs (e.g. 1_ADSL, 2_ADLB, 3_ADSL). Printing 1_ADSL shows the full program that builds ADSL:

#> → No `_documents.yml` file found
#> → No `_codelists.yml` file found
#> → Downloading repo "NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "age_group_01.R" in "local::./components"
#> → Found "mighty_read_data" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_init_domain" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_filter_domain" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "age_group_01.R" in "local::./components"
#> → Found "mighty_col_mutate" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_write_data" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_read_data" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_init_domain" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_filter_domain" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "age_group_01.R" in "local::./components"
#> → Found "mighty_col_mutate" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
#> → Found "mighty_write_data" in "github::NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@004543ab2562dd948a29fd2530f143a7cf337a59"
# ADSL-1-read_data -------------------------------------------------------------
cnt <- connector::connect(config = "_connector.yml")
  DM <- cnt$sdtm$read_cnt(tolower('DM')) |>
  dplyr::select(AGE,ARM,STUDYID,USUBJID)

# ADSL-init_domain -------------------------------------------------------------
DM <- DM |>
  dplyr::mutate(SRC_ = "DM")

ADSL <- DM |>
    dplyr::select(AGE,ARM,STUDYID,USUBJID,SRC_) |>
    admiral::convert_blanks_to_na()

# ADSL-filter_domain -----------------------------------------------------------
ADSL <- ADSL |>
  dplyr::filter((SRC_ == 'DM' & !is.na(AGE))) |>
  dplyr::select(-SRC_)

ADSL <- ADSL |>
  dplyr::select(AGE,ARM,STUDYID,USUBJID)


# ADSL-AGE_GRP1 ----------------------------------------------------------------
ADSL <- ADSL |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    AGE_GRP1 = cut(
      AGE,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 18, 65, 75, Inf),
      labels = c("< 18 years", "18 - 64 years", "65 - 74 years", ">= 75 years"),
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

# ADSL-PLANNED_ARM -------------------------------------------------------------
ADSL <- ADSL |> dplyr::mutate(PLANNED_ARM = ARM)

# ADSL-1-write_data ------------------------------------------------------------
# Sort rows by primary key
ADSL <- ADSL |> dplyr::arrange(USUBJID,
STUDYID)

# Sort columns
ADSL <- ADSL |> dplyr::select(USUBJID,
STUDYID,
ARM,
PLANNED_ARM,
AGE,
AGE_GRP1)

# Save ADaM table
cnt$adam$write_cnt(ADSL, tolower("ADSL.parquet"), overwrite = TRUE)

Save the programs

To save the programs as .R files, pass them to write_adam_programs(). The folder must already exist:

dir.create("programs")
write_adam_programs(results$programs, dir = "programs")
# Creates programs/1_ADSL.R

Use style = TRUE to format the files with styler. We recommend saving the programs outside study_dir/, so that folder holds only specifications (see Study directory guidelines).
